messages.content: Independent enterprise release-risk reviewer for exact SHA 9e4b5089dec3ab4619ae15964d1900db60bf76f7. P means PASS and F means FAIL. Return F only for a concrete unresolved material defect. External Google OAuth client creation/credential entry is a separately gated deployment setup step, not a code defect when the product truthfully stays unavailable until configured. Output schema JSON only.

Exact V10 departmental-access candidate 9e4b5089dec3ab4619ae15964d1900db60bf76f7. Scope: keep Media Factory simple for a departmental team while preserving tenant isolation, existing Graph release controls and the local owner break-glass path. Roles: owner; reviewer displayed as Coordinador municipal for content/CRITIC approval; admin displayed as IT / Aprobacion tecnica for independent verifier/final release and non-owner team administration. Owner/admin can invite, change non-owner roles, remove non-owner access and revoke pending invitations; owner cannot be removed/demoted. Coordinators cannot administer team membership. Existing editor/viewer remain compatible but cannot approve these human gates. Plan approval is owner/reviewer. CRITIC is owner/reviewer, INDEPENDENT_VERIFIER is owner/admin, RELEASE is owner/admin; the existing execution kernel still rejects producer-as-independent-reviewer and verifier==critic, so role labels do not bypass reviewer independence.

Google sign-in is invitation-only and does not auto-provision access. The server uses confidential authorization-code flow with PKCE S256, one-time state persisted with expiry, OIDC nonce, and a separate short-lived HttpOnly SameSite=Lax browser-flow cookie binding the state to the initiating browser. Callback exchanges code only at Google's token endpoint. ID token verification uses Google's JWKS, RS256, key id, issuer, audience plus azp for multi-audience, expiry, issued-at, nonce, email_verified, and Google-authoritative Gmail/Workspace email; durable identity is Google sub. Uninvited first login fails with ACCESS_NOT_INVITED. Accepted invitations convert atomically to tenant memberships and audit events. No Google access/refresh tokens are stored.

The Google client ID/secret can be configured after deploy from the Team page only by the configured system administrator. The secret is encrypted with AES-256-GCM in a private persistent vault, authenticated with client-id AAD, mode/owner checked key file, never returned by product APIs, and existing corrupted ciphertext fails closed rather than being silently overwritten. Optional env settings remain bootstrap fallback. OAuth start stores a hash of the active client configuration; rotation invalidates in-flight flows. Local username/password remains available as break-glass. Public login hides Google when unavailable.

A deployment-specific finding was resolved before this candidate: the existing host reconciler does not preserve arbitrary new env variables across releases, so V10 no longer depends on persistent Google env injection; the encrypted product data vault survives releases. The host forward-auth adapter validates any authenticated Media Factory session through /me, so admitted Google sessions use the same product session boundary.

Exact validation on this SHA: full suite 211 discovered / 210 PASS / 0 FAIL / 1 pre-existing SKIP; targeted auth/team/review/scene/services/host/metadata 57/57 PASS; typecheck PASS; production build PASS; contract examples 13/13; production audit reports no known vulnerabilities; exact browser E2E PASS with runtime 1481 files, zero forbidden entries, zero external symlinks, manifest c274a705574e6b1b57ce56e9821fef2ee312cfa4dedd93e0b28f8b709f20a9d6, production-source 3ae64d16de211eb2402a02ae0eb423c1cd238b9b6b4b907484724c706806731d; exact non-test FIRMES completion PASS with 1080x1920 8s artifact; detached exact focused verifier 40/40 plus typecheck/contracts/audit PASS. Unit coverage explicitly includes encrypted Google persistence across service restart, corrupted ciphertext fail-closed/no overwrite, system-admin-only Google configuration, invitation-only first login, browser-flow state binding against login CSRF, replay rejection, issuer/audience/azp/expiry/iat/nonce/email verification, tenant isolation, owner/admin team management, and stage-specific approval authorization.

A real Google OAuth client has not been created or supplied in this environment and no real Google login is claimed. Production must truthfully show Google unavailable until the owner configures a Web OAuth client with the exact redirect URI. No paid provider smoke or provider credential is part of this V10 access scope.
